title: Month-over-Month Revenue Change Using LAG
description:
Calculate the revenue change compared to the previous month for each month in the dataset.

**Table: monthly_revenue** — `month`, `revenue`

Output columns: `month`, `revenue`, `prev_revenue`, `change`. Order by `month`.
solution_sql: SELECT month, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_revenue, revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change FROM monthly_revenue ORDER BY month

test_cases.description: 8 months; first row has NULL prev_revenue; 7 rows show a meaningful change value

hints: LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) returns the revenue value from the preceding row in the ordered window.
The first row will have NULL for prev_revenue and change since there is no prior period.
explanation: LAG(col) looks at the previous row value. For Jan: prev_revenue=NULL, change=NULL. For Feb: prev_revenue=50000, change=+5000. For Mar: prev_revenue=55000, change=-7000. This pattern enables period-over-period comparisons without a self-join.
